records.claim: Counterexample to hazard-rate extension of Theorem 6 (p. 160)
records.quote: A natural question which arises here is whether the results in Theorems 6 and 7 can be extended, respectively, to the hazard rate and likelihood ratio orders. Unfortunately, the answer is no as shown in the following examples. Set n = 3, ν = 0.5, τ = 0.2, α = β = (4.5, 2, 3), λ = (9, 3.5, 0.1) and μ = (10, 2.9, 0.3). We then find F̄X3:3 (4)/F̄Y3:3 (4) = 1.13809, F̄X3:3 (5)/F̄Y3:3 (5) = 1.14207, F̄X3:3 (15)/F̄Y3:3 (15) = 1.12199. This observation means that the ratio of the survival functions of X3:3 and Y3:3 is not monotone, i.e., the lifetimes of Systems A and B can not be compared in the sense of the hazard rate order. However, log μ ≺^w_α log λ on D3 and α ≺^uo β.
